key_insight: In a small proof-of-concept study, GPT-5 reconstructed pregnancy episodes from clinical notes more completely and with more accurate dates than an ICD-code algorithm.
clinical_relevance: Narrative-based extraction could improve pregnancy identification and characterization for maternal and fetal health research.
method: Provided GPT-5 with chronologically concatenated clinical notes and messages.
Extracted pregnancy episodes, dates, outcomes, complications, and reproductive-treatment details.
Compared results with manual chart review and a hierarchical ICD-code algorithm.
evidence_signal: Among 54 pregnancies in 20 held-out patients, GPT-5 identified 53 versus 40 for the code algorithm, with 3 versus 24 spurious episodes and detection F1 scores of 0.96 versus 0.68.
watch_item: Different input data prevent attributing gains solely to the LLM; validation in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is needed.
paper_title: Beyond billing codes: a proof-of-concept study of large language models for pregnancy episode reconstruction from clinical notes
